transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. I'm Dennis. I guess... I've just been having some issues with eating lately. 

It's kind of hard to explain, but... once I start eating sometimes, it feels like I hit some switch. And I just keep going. Even while part of me is in my head thinking, like, Dennis, just stop already. But I don't. 

So... yeah. That's why I'm here.

After you eat, especially after one of these episodes where you feel like you can't stop, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot to try to control your weight or what you ate?
Um... no. I don't do any of that. I just... I just eat.
During these episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating, do you feel like you're not in control of what or how much you're eating?

Yeah... um, like I was saying earlier, it's... it's just like a switch flips. I know in my head I should stop, but I just... don't. So... yeah. I guess I don't really feel like I'm in control when it happens.
How often do these episodes happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say you lose control and keep eating even when you don’t want to?

Um... I guess it happens most weeks. Usually just one night, maybe two. It's been like that since early in the semester, so... maybe three or four months now. Usually when I have a lot of deadlines or there's just a lot of food around the apartment.
Do these episodes where you lose control while eating bother you or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Um... I mean, I guess it bothers me. But it hasn't really knocked me off track or anything. I'm still making it to class... and robotics. 

It's just... sometimes the next morning I feel kind of sluggish. Or distracted, I guess. And... I don't know, I just spend extra time worrying if my roommates noticed anything. So... yeah. It bothers me more than it actually stops me from doing stuff.
During these episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean, I eat pretty fast. Usually I'm just standing by my desk, trying to get back to homework or a game or whatever. I don't really... I don't really taste it. It's just kind of gone in a few minutes before I even realize it.
During these episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating, do you usually eat until you feel uncomfortably full?

Um... yeah. I guess so. I usually only stop when... I don't know, when my stomach just feels really tight. And heavy. It gets to the point where I'm just uncomfortable sitting there at my desk anymore, so... I usually have to go lie down for a while.
Do you find yourself eating a definitely larger amount of food in one sitting than most people would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances?

Um... yeah, I suppose. Like, if it's after a big project deadline... or if someone left pizza out in the kitchen. I might take some to my room and just... keep going. I'll finish a whole small pizza, and then maybe chips, or cereal. It's... definitely more than my roommates eat for dinner. And more than I meant to eat when I started.
Have these episodes ever caused you significant distress or affected your relationships, schoolwork, or other important areas of your life?

Um... I don't know if it's significant, exactly. I still go to class. I still go to my robotics club. But... I guess I feel pretty sluggish the next morning sometimes. And... I don't know, I just spend a lot of time worrying if my roommates noticed how much I took, or if they heard me in the kitchen. It... it bothers me, but it hasn't really stopped me from doing what I need to do, I guess.
Do these episodes usually happen when you're feeling upset, stressed, or experiencing a low mood?
Um... I guess so. Sometimes. Like if I'm stressed about a test or something, maybe. But I don't really know if that's the only time. It just... happens.
